$comment: Form-structure profile (task 5.1). Presentation CONVENTIONS keyed by structural kind, criterion-independent — the counterpart of encoding-profile.json for the form lens. R6.2: filledBy follows the leaf kind (REQUIREMENT is authored by the contracting authority in the REQUEST, QUESTION is answered by the economic operator in the RESPONSE). R6.3: visibleWhen follows the condition marker. R6.4: codelist comes from the value-type registry shape. uiType defaults and i18n keys are added in task 5.2.

filledBy.$comment: R6.2 — leaf nodeKind -> role that fills the field.
filledBy.$comment.mixed: A group whose leaves are all one role carries that role; a criterion (or group) spanning both roles carries 'both'.

visibleWhen.$comment: R6.3 — condition marker -> the boolean the gating leaf must hold. The gate is the nearest preceding sibling value leaf of the conditional group, the same rule the instance-data generator uses for if/then/else (task 4.3.2).
visibleWhen.$comment.requiredIsScopedToVisibility: `required` on a gated field means 'required ONCE SHOWN', matching the generated schema, whose derived if/then requires the field inside the branch. Note the hand-authored part-IV.form.json is inconsistent on this point (evidence[].url is required:true with a visibleWhen, while reliedUpon is required:false with one); the generator applies the schema-consistent rule uniformly.
visibleWhen.$comment.nearestGateOnly: Only the NEAREST conditional ancestor produces a visibleWhen, not the whole ancestor chain. Deeper gates are transitively satisfied: a gate that is itself hidden stays unanswered, so it cannot hold the value that reveals its children. This matches the hand-authored lens.

uiType.$comment: R10.2 / R6.5 — default uiType table keyed by ValueDataTypeCode, so the common case needs no per-field authoring. An object-shaped value type maps PER PROPERTY (an AMOUNT is a number input plus a currency picker). A value type absent from this table has no inferable control and MUST be supplied by the presentation sidecar, otherwise the build fails with the component's semantic ID (R6.7).
uiType.$comment.descriptionDefault: DESCRIPTION defaults to multi-line 'textarea' because most ESPD free-text requirements are prose. Short single-line DESCRIPTION fields (e.g. an entity name) are the documented override case for the presentation sidecar — this is exactly the ambiguity R6.5 anticipates.

i18n.$comment: R6.6 — label/title keys. FINDING: these are DERIVABLE, contrary to the original R10 assumption. The shipped catalogue under i18n/i18n/en/ is already keyed by '<kind>.label.<criterion-code>.<EA tag path>', i.e. the requestpath with its leading 'C31_' segment replaced by the criterion code. All 17 C31 leaf keys plus the criterion name/description resolve this way, so no sidecar authoring is needed for labels. The sidecar is only needed for property-level sub-labels (see propertyLabelKeys) because the catalogue is LEAF-level: one key per leaf, even where the form renders several inputs for that leaf (a PERIOD has a single key, 'Start date; End date').

grouping.$comment: Form groups are derived, not hand-named: all REQUIREMENT leaves form the buyer group, and each top-level QUESTION group under the criterion forms one response group. The group id is the instance-path segment the group's leaves share (giving turnover/startTrading/electronicEvidence for C31); where they share none, the first leaf's leading segment is used. EA tags (QSG1, ...) are deliberately NOT used as ids — they are encoding artefacts with no place in a presentation lens. A nicer name for a prefix-less group (the hand-authored C31 lens calls QSG1 'fulfilment') is a presentation decision and belongs in the task 5.2 presentation sidecar.
